subtopics.title: How Mining Built and Still Carries South Africa

questions.question: Johannesburg grew from farmland to the subcontinent's largest city because of:
The JSE belongs in the "mining built the economy" evidence chain because it was:
Mining's outsized modern contribution lies especially in:
options: Employing most of the national workforce
Merchandise export earnings that pay for imports

questions.question: Acid mine drainage, dust, sinkholes and stranded mining towns belong to:

subtopics.title: The Platinum Case Study: Location and Favouring Factors

questions.question: South Africa's platinum lies in the:
The western limb of the platinum belt runs through:
options: The Rustenburg and Brits districts of North West

questions.question: The two platinum-bearing horizons the mines follow are:
options: The Main Reef and Black Reef
The Merensky Reef and the UG2 chromitite layer

questions.question: A market factor favouring platinum mining is:
options: Falling world demand for all metals
Global demand for autocatalysts that clean vehicle exhausts
The absence of substitutes for coal

subtopics.title: Platinum's Contribution and Its Hindering Factors

questions.question: Within South African mining, the platinum industry is notable as the:
options: Largest employer, on the order of 170 000 direct workers

questions.question: Beneficiation means:
options: Processing ore locally to add value before export
Exporting raw ore as fast as possible

questions.question: A PHYSICAL/TECHNICAL hindering factor for platinum mining is:
options: Thin, deep reefs that are hot, labour-intensive and hard to mechanise

questions.question: Battery electric vehicles pose a long-term demand risk because they:

subtopics.title: Mining on the Map: Identification, Grid References and Symbols

questions.question: Which combination is strong map evidence of mining activity?
options: Contour lines and a trigonometrical beacon
A vineyard symbol and a farm dam
Mine dumps with straight edges, a dead-end railway spur and converging power lines
Green vegetation shading along a river

questions.question: In a six-figure grid reference, the correct reading order is:
options: Eastings first, then northings — along the corridor, then up the stairs

questions.question: On topographic maps, blue, green and brown respectively indicate:
Asked WHY mining locates at a mapped Rustenburg site, your explanation should draw on:
options: The platinum case study — Bushveld reefs, infrastructure, labour and world demand

subtopics.title: The Country That Dug Itself Into Existence

questions.question: "Follow any thread of the modern economy backwards and you arrive at a mine" refers to:
options: Railways, Eskom, the JSE and Johannesburg all growing to serve mining
Mining being the largest sector today

questions.question: Mining as "the family member working overseas" captures its role in:
options: Earning foreign exchange through exports to balance the country's account

questions.question: "When a mine dies, its town is stranded" because mining towns:
options: Were built for one purpose and lose their reason to exist

subtopics.title: The Buried Saucer Full of Platinum

questions.question: In the saucer picture, the platinum-rich layers formed when:
options: Cooling molten rock settled its minerals into flat layers

questions.question: The permanent name-pairing for the capital of platinum country is:
The four "lucky cards" in South Africa's platinum hand are:
options: Rich deposit, ready skills, nearby infrastructure, hungry market
Cheap power, flat land, many rivers, mild climate

questions.question: Mining "a coin locked inside a slab" describes reefs that are:
options: Thin — about a metre — and very deep, so hard to mechanise

questions.question: "Shapes nature refuses to make" — straight-edged pale mounds and square dams — are:
A railway spur dead-ending at buildings in open veld suggests mining because:
options: Only heavy, valuable rock justifies rails to an isolated works
Stations must be far from towns

questions.question: The chant "along the corridor, then up the stairs" orders:
options: Easting then northing in a grid reference

questions.question: "Never memorise in a panic what the legend will hand you free" means:
options: Symbols change on every sheet randomly
The symbol key is printed on the sheet — your job is speed, not recall
Legends are not printed on exam maps
Colours have no meaning on maps
